title: Validation attributes and ProblemDetails
summary: Put data annotations on a request DTO and let [ApiController] return a 400 ProblemDetails before the action runs.

scenario.briefing: The product create action accepts a blank name and a negative stock because the request record has no constraints. Add a validation contract and return a proper 201 when the request is accepted.

objectives.description: Declare constraints on the request DTO and bind it to an API action.
Explain when model validation runs and what response it produces.
Predict the result for an invalid numeric range.

hints: Data annotations belong on the request record, not on the entity.
Use Required and StringLength on the name, and Range on the stock.
Return Created with a location and the created product.

misconceptions.description: Expecting model binding to reject invalid values with no constraints.
misconceptions.testDescription: The request record declares its validation contract.
misconceptions.feedback: Model binding converts types; it does not invent business rules. Attributes declare the rules that ModelState checks.

misconceptions.description: Adding a manual ModelState check in every action.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Believing ModelState.IsValid must be checked by hand even on an API controller.
misconceptions.feedback: [ApiController] installs a filter that short-circuits invalid ModelState with a 400 ProblemDetails response.

misconceptions.description: Assuming [Required] rejects the default value of a value type.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that [Required] rejects 0 on a non-nullable int.
misconceptions.feedback: A non-nullable int always has a value, so [Required] passes. Use [Range] to reject an out-of-range number.
Range is enforced during model validation. The negative value never reaches the action.

misconceptions.description: Expecting a 500 for an invalid client value.
misconceptions.feedback: A validation failure is a client error and returns 400. A 500 means the server failed after accepting the request.

sections.title: Attributes declare the contract
sections.body: Data annotations such as [Required], [StringLength], and [Range] sit on the request DTO. They describe the boundary before any business logic runs. Keeping them on the DTO also keeps the entity free of transport rules.

sections.title: [ApiController] supplies the validation response
sections.body: The attribute adds API conventions, including automatic model validation. When ModelState is invalid, the framework returns 400 with a ValidationProblemDetails body before the action method executes. A manual ModelState check in every action is redundant.

sections.title: A successful create is 201
sections.body: Created returns 201 and a location for the new resource. Returning Ok after a create hides the fact that a resource was created and gives the client no location to follow.

steps.title: What the API controller filter does
hints: Think about what happens between model binding and the action body.
The filter runs for every action on an API controller.
A non-nullable value type always has a value.
ProblemDetails is a normal response body, not a debug view.

statements.label: [ApiController] returns 400 with ProblemDetails when ModelState is invalid.
Data annotations are evaluated before the action body runs.
[Required] rejects the value 0 on a non-nullable int property.
Every action must check ModelState.IsValid even with [ApiController].
ProblemDetails includes the exception stack trace by default.

steps.explanation: The API controller filter short-circuits invalid model state with a 400 ProblemDetails response. Annotations run during binding, before the action. [Required] cannot reject 0 on a non-nullable int, and the default ProblemDetails body does not expose a stack trace.

steps.title: Transfer to a negative range
steps.prompt: A client posts a product with Stock = -1. The record declares [Range(0, 100000)] and the controller has [ApiController]. Which response is produced?
hints: Range is a validation attribute, not a type conversion.
The API controller filter runs before the action.
An out-of-range value makes ModelState invalid.
Invalid model state becomes 400, not 500 or 201.

quiz.prompt: A client posts a product with Stock = -1. The record declares [Range(0, 100000)] and the controller has [ApiController]. Which response is produced?

options.label: 400 with ProblemDetails before the action runs.
201 because Range only applies to query-string parameters.
500 because the negative value reaches the service.
200 with the stored product; Range is documentation only.

quiz.explanation: Range fails for -1, ModelState becomes invalid, and the API controller filter returns 400 ProblemDetails before Create runs.
